Repo copies, cached copies, local settings, a signed-out session or a read older than two check periods are red. Library: `framework/libs/hubstatus` (`hubLive` in `core.ts`).
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).

No look or layout value is decided in a component or a stylesheet alone: it comes from an asset through the engines' tokens. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.

"If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.

## What a Blueprint is
A named package of plans in Plan Studio, like build profiles but for plans. Only one blueprint is active at a time; Plan Studio shows only the active blueprint's plans. Plans keep their exact structure (steps, sub-items, status, build links) inside a blueprint.

3. **Context menu**: Plan Studio's context menu gets a **Blueprints** submenu listing every blueprint; selecting one switches the active blueprint. Same switch available via control@1 (planner.blueprints list/add/act switch), MCP, CLI and voice ("switch blueprint to X").

postgres-console.brief:
# Postgres: ONE true location for all data sets, in its own container (Brett, Nov 7)

Orchestrator build id: `postgres-console` (profile all, 7 steps) with Plan Studio plan `postgres-for-the-console-orchestrator-id-registr-anyx` — read both (`node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs brief postgres-console`) and follow them, with this change: Postgres runs in its OWN Docker container, not inside the console's.

Problem: the same data lives in 3+ places (builds store, per-profile orchestrator files, pending list, journal, plans, tracker/catalog, feature-ledger, origins) read by different tools, constantly out of sync.

1. Contract (Fable): schema for builds, steps, plans, blueprints, journal, queue, accounts/workers usage, Shipped features, origins, ID registry (orchestrator assigns every id). Migrations versioned.
2. Own container: `axf-postgres` (official image, pinned), internal Docker network only (no public port), named data volume, healthcheck, restart policy, nightly backup + restore script, credentials in the vault/env (never in git). Compose/deploy files + docs.
3. Importer: every existing JSON source loaded losslessly, counts/hashes verified, duplicates resolved with a report.
4. Switch every reader/writer (orchestrator, Build manager, Builds page, Plan Studio, builds-live, merge queue, MCP/CLI, AmberX, axHub) to the DB. JSON files become generated read-only exports for git/sessions. Kill file locks.
5. CI check: no code writes those JSON files directly anymore.
6. Tests + perf check. Add to Shipped features.

Deploying the container is a VPS write: prepare it, and leave a one-command deploy for Brett/orchestrator. Progress: append `<time> START|DONE <step>` to PROGRESS.md here at each step; don't stop between steps. Commit, don't push.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.
- Plugin Manager (Oct 18 2026; Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026): the console's plugin manager is the `plugin-manager` plugin; its model is the cross-port `plugin-inventory@1` engine (`framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` = Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` = the plugin's `server/engine.py`, one fixture). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. The console already has the **Build profiles** plugin (`build-profiles`: dialog + settings tab, banner chip, switch/create/rename/remove) over `framework/cli/profiles.mjs` (build-profiles@1) and the builds store. Grow THAT plugin into a full manager page (rename the plugin title to 'Build profiles' manager if needed; keep its id, data and every existing feature).

## Features
- **Browse:** framework grid of every profile (collapsible rows): name, id, active star, description, counts (builds running / pending / complete / archived, pending items, queue steps), cost spent + cost left, last activity, created; sort/search/filter. Expand a row: its builds (with agent avatars once crew-live lands), pending list, queue, plan summary, files (`profiles.mjs where`).
- **View** a profile page: all its builds and steps, timeline, totals, links to Builds page views filtered to it.
- **Create** (name, id, description, copy from another profile, catalog on/off, make active), **Edit** (name, description, catalog, colour/icon for the banner chip), **Switch** (one tap; banner chip + context menu), **Duplicate**, **Merge** two profiles, **Move builds** between profiles (multi-select, drag rows onto a profile), **Archive / hide**, **Delete** = take off the list (data kept, restorable) with confirm; a separate 'Delete data too' that is owner-only and irreversible-confirm. Base profile and active profile can't be deleted.
- **Cleanup helper:** flag archived builds that are actually complete (reconciler) - e.g. angel, big-dog, breakroom, refactor - with a one-tap fix.

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. Nightly console deploy: `deploy/console-nightly.mjs` (Claude settings `nightly.*`). `console.refresh`: `axf console refresh [--hard]`.
- Feature status: framework/catalog/status.json, then `node framework/cli/tracker.mjs`. Heavy steps (npm/vite builds, Playwright) go through `node framework/cli/agent-slots.mjs heavy -- <cmd>`.
- Console control (Nov 13 2026): every screen, tab, setting, button, function, plugin, grid row and build step of the console has an address (`view:settings/tab:settings.tabs=plugins`, `setting:…`, `row:<build>/step:s3`) and is driven the same way through REST `/api/console-control`, the `console_control_*` MCP tools, `axf console …` and AmberX voice (Ctrl+K searches it in the console). New UI registers its targets through the framework controls or `data-axf-target`; `framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs` fails CI otherwise. Approve / deny and owner-only settings are never commands; destructive presses need `confirm`. Doc `_claude/memory/docs/console-control.md`, contract `framework/spec/CONSOLE-CONTROL.md`.
- Patches and Build Pilot are retired (Nov 3 2026): both apps and every integration with them were removed; the Dev Console and every other app run standalone. `MossesX/Build-Pilot` is archived on GitHub (read-only). Report `_claude/builds/reports/kill-patches-pilot.md`.
- No secrets: `AXF_TOKEN` and `GITHUB_TOKEN` are environment variables only. `.mcp.json` references `${AXF_TOKEN}`.
- He works mostly from his phone (Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra), often in Moshi (mosh) on his Hostinger VPS where Claude Code runs. Lead with the result, short paragraphs, phone-readable.
- Everything a later session needs lives in `_claude/` (this project) or `_claude/shared/` (all projects), synced with the hub. Phone, VPS, desktop and claude.ai sessions don't share chat history.
- GitHub: account `MossesX`. A new repo must exist on GitHub before a session can push to it.
- axHub (`MossesX/axHub`, https://axhub.amberxai.com/mcp) is his connector hub: use its tools (`list_services`, `describe_service`, `call`) to reach his services instead of asking for credentials.
- Pending builds: check the pending list before any build (`node framework/cli/pending.mjs`, MCP `pending_list`, console → Pending builds). "Add to the pending build list" means park it.
- Check the queue for clashes, and build related items together (Oct 21 2026, Brett): whenever any session (any machine, any surface: VPS, cloud, headless, claude.ai, console launches) is asked to build anything or to put anything in the build queue, first go through everything still to build (pending list, build queue, plan; the console's Build manager shows them all) for items that touch the same files, features or contracts, or that would later conflict with, undo or redo what is being built. If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Screenshots that aren't for approval go to Screenshots, not the review queue (Nov 1 2026, Brett): a session checking a screen (e.g. the Breakroom), live captures, PR before/after and other ad-hoc pictures are saved with `axf shot <file> --name "…" --app <app> --screen <route> --group "…"` (`node framework/cli/shot.mjs`, or `POST /api/plugins/ui-review/shots`), which lands in UI Review → Screenshots and never waits for approve / reject; Brett can still *Send to review* one. Only planned UI goes through `review.mjs submit`.
- Every tab group, toolbar, banner and nav menu is an asset with an asset settings interface (Nov 4 2026, Brett; shared rule of the same name; build `tab-group-assets`): every tab row in the console, Molly, AmberX web and axHub web is the framework `TabGroup` on the `tab-group` asset (per-row pick `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>.asset`, per-row overrides `axf.chrome.tab-group.<id>`); right-click / long-press any tab group, toolbar, banner, nav or menu bar → Settings… / Change… / Move (`framework/react/components/ChromeContext.tsx`, dialogs `axf.chrome.settings` + `axf.chrome.pick`). Settings dialogs render through the `settings` asset picked for the kind (`axf.chrome.settings.<type>`; the shared default `settings/chrome-<type>` unless the app's copy `settings/chrome-<type>-<app>` is picked; `extends` folds the chain). Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). A strip that must stay hand-drawn (the Terminal tab strip, the workspace pane strip) carries `data-axf-tab-group="<id>"` + `data-fx-ctx-target="tab-group"`; anything else is a finding in `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`, whose ratchet `framework/spec/chrome-baseline.json` only comes down (`--write-baseline` after a real migration). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.

I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.

The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.

Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).

- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.

Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fable-review-6xha`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.

If any of them should be built at the same time, build them together in this build (tell Brett which ones and why before starting; when one of them is pinned to a different model, say so in the model pick), then take each one off the pending list / build queue (mark it complete with this build's branch/PR and tick its steps) so nothing is built twice. If an item would clash but shouldn't be built now, say so and add a note on that item. When adding to the queue, merge into an overlapping item instead of adding a duplicate.
- Every veto notice says what it's for (Oct 26 2026, Brett; axHub decision #99; veto since Oct 30 2026, #103): every axHub call that changes something carries `reason: { title, description }` (title = what is about to happen, one plain line; description = what it does and why). The notice and the AXHub page show the title first, the description when expanded, and the exact code in its own collapsible section; a call without a reason is refused.
- One session, no sub-agents, no fan-outs. Don't ask questions: nobody is watching. Pick the sensible option, say so in the PR.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.
- Deleting files on the hub through axHub is a veto call (runs after the countdown unless Brett denies it).
- axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.

Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.
- Plugins a host makes unneeded aren't loaded (Oct 22 2026, Brett): when an app runs inside a host (any app in a host's tab), plugins that would draw something the host already draws, or that the host makes unnecessary, aren't loaded on that page and are logged at launch. - axHub calls that change something carry `reason: {title, description}`. Send once and keep working: no polling, no re-sending, never approve anything yourself. Every run on an API key is Brett's confirm approval, never a veto.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. In AmberX-AXF the place is the systems check's health@1 registry (`plugin_services.get("axf.health@1").register(…)`, `apps/console-web/plugins/systems-check/README.md`); a new key, service or failure mode gets a live check there.
- Shared data is on the hub: the root manifest's `data.shared` (pending list, plan + media, build queue, catalog status, libraries index, project rules, tracker) is read and written in `/projects/amberx-axf/_data/<same path as in the repo>` where `/projects` is mounted (the Dev Console container), through `framework/cli/persist.mjs`. The repo copies are synced snapshots (`claude-sync sync`, then commit). On the VPS, change data through the CLI, console or MCP, not by editing repo files.
- Plugins: each plugin gets a Plugin Manager entry (info, enable/disable, logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen, and never get a top-level settings tab: each plugin's settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins (`SettingsTab.parent = 'plugins'`, enforced by the console for every plugin).
- Every plugin ships install.mjs + uninstall.mjs and a Plugin Manager entry. Check: `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check <folder>`.
- UI-editing plugins: last save wins, fresh on focus (Oct 18 2026): theme, style, layout, manager and builder plugins (`plugin.json` → `uiEditor`: theme/style/layout/manager/builder) may edit the same values. Saves are per key, and when two of them save the same key the last save wins (`SettingsRegistry.set` merges into what storage holds now, so a save never reverts other keys). Whenever one opens, loads or comes back into focus (window focus, tab visible, another tab saved), it reloads current token values from settings before showing them: `useEditorSync()` (`framework/react/editorSync.ts`) → `rt.refreshFromSaved()` (web) / `AxfRuntime.refreshFromSaved()` (Kotlin). Two enabled editors of one kind are shown as an info-level clash in the Plugin Manager, not an error.

It opens each plugin's UI and settings when they exist and lists dependencies in detail (what it needs and whether it's met, who provides it, who needs it, clashes). Every app's Settings → Plugins tab lists its libraries from the same engine; Android ships `PluginManagerModule` (axf-devtools). Links in menus are runtime contributions (`AxfWebLibrary.contextMenu`, `rt.addContextItems`), never edits to a context-menu asset.
- One banner on screen — embed@1 (Oct 21 2026, Brett): an app shown inside another app's frame hides the chrome the host shows, its banner by default. Hosts mark what they embed (`EmbedEngine.userAgentSuffix` on a WebView's user agent, or `embedUrl` → `?axf-embed=<host>`); guests detect it (`rt.embedded`, automatic on the web) and apply the hide engine's forced layer, never touching the user's own saved choice. Settings grey the slot out ("Shown by <host>"). No app hosts others today (Patches, the first host, was retired Nov 3 2026). Engines on both ports, fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.
- One Banners settings (Oct 22 2026, Brett): every banner plugin's settings are one interface (Settings → Plugins → Banners and the right-click Banner settings: a tab per banner with its look, behaviour and own settings). A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.
- Plugins a host makes unneeded aren't loaded (Oct 22 2026, Brett): when an app runs inside a host (any app in a host's tab), plugins that would draw something the host already draws, or that the host makes unnecessary, aren't loaded on that page and are logged at launch. A plugin says when in its web library: `embed: { skipWhen: ['embedded' | 'take:<fn>' | 'hidden:<type>'] }` (`embedSkipReason` in `framework/core/engines/embed.ts`); `installLibraries` skips it, `rt.skippedLibraries` keeps why, the terminal gets one line each plus a summary, Settings → Plugins lists them. Page mode (an app's settings page in the host) never skips. Standalone everything loads. Every new plugin that only draws on chrome a host hides, or does a job a host takes, declares it.

- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.

Every app in `framework/schemas/shared-assets.json` + Expenses carries its six copies (`node framework/cli/chrome-settings.mjs check` in CI; `backfill` writes missing ones). Report: `_claude/builds/reports/tab-group-assets.md`.
- Every project has `_claude/` (memory/, instructions/, rules/, shared/) synced with `/projects/<name>/_claude/`, and its manifest's `data.shared` files synced with `/projects/<name>/_data/<same path>`.

New app subdomains are A records to the VPS (31.97.13.252, like the others). Every change (and any check that answered a question) gets a line in the DNS log on axHub: `/projects/_shared/_data/dns/log.md` (`axhub.memory_read`/`memory_write`, project `shared`, area `data`, path `dns/log.md`): date/time (UTC), what (record, type, value, TTL), why (which app or question), who (session/surface), result. Never delete or overwrite other records without asking him.
- Don't hand Brett chores (Oct 21 2026, Brett): anything a session would otherwise ask him to do (DNS records, env vars, redeploys, installers, VPS commands) the session does itself through axHub (`vps.run` as a veto call, the hub's other services). Anything that truly can't be done that way goes into the console's systems check banner as an item with Auto fix, like the other checks, instead of a to-do list in chat.
- Broken = a banner item with a fix (Oct 30 2026, Brett: "You need to make sure things like that go into one of the banners. I need to see that kind of shit."): anything broken that Brett needs to know about or fix (a dead, expired or under-scoped key, a service that stopped answering, a stuck build, CI red on main, a container in a restart loop, a full disk, a denied or expired approval) goes into a console banner item that says in plain words what broke, what it breaks and since when, with a Fix or Auto fix button, and is pushed once to the AmberX app. Never only in chat, a log or a terminal line. Settings grey the slot out ("Shown by <host>"). No app hosts others today (Patches, the first host, was retired Nov 3 2026). Engines on both ports, fixture `spec/fixtures/embed.json`.
- One Banners settings (Oct 22 2026, Brett): every banner plugin's settings are one interface (Settings → Plugins → Banners and the right-click Banner settings: a tab per banner with its look, behaviour and own settings). A new banner plugin declares `label`, `icon` and `settingsTab` on its banner so its settings join in.

- AmberX-AXF is private. Don't create the separate console repo (`axf-console`, reserved in its manifest) until he says so.
- Attached things snap, never overlap (Oct 28 2026, Brett): anything attached to a host (banner, toolbar, menubar; plugin badges, widgets, popups) never draws over or clips a neighbour. Sides size to their content, the flexible piece (search bar) shrinks to its minimum first, and a full host scrolls sideways with scroll snap. New hosts and new widget kinds follow the same rule (`framework/ui/axf.css`, banner section).
- Every settings interface keeps its level toolbar; plugin settings are a sub-tab of Settings → Plugins.
- Everything in the UI is an asset, and an asset change reaches every app (Oct 30 2026, Brett): any part of the UI that should be changeable is an asset (`asset@1`) — make a new asset type when none fits (asset-types.json, validators, engine, fixture; Fable for the contract). Assets are shared through the axHub look, so changing one changes every app on the framework live. Build `ui-all-assets` (Angel) does the existing UI; every new UI follows it from now on.
- The look comes from axHub only, and every app ships every shareable asset (Nov 1 2026, Brett: "The apps should only get appearance from axhub period." "If you select design package in one app it changes it for all! Any theme change applies to all." "They all gotta ship all assets that can be shared bruh!"): no opt-out switch, no look tabs or scopes that draw an app under a look that isn't the hub's, no local fallback. Every look change in any app (design package, slot, spacing, hidden chrome, Sliders, per-asset tokens) goes to the one appearance@1 document and applies in every app. Every listed app (`framework/schemas/shared-assets.json`: Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX) ships the whole shared set baked at `src/axf/assets` (`node framework/cli/shared-assets.mjs bake|check`, CI); an app's `src/assets` holds only what is truly its own, `src/assets-overrides` the shared ids it tunes. A new asset that more than one app could use goes in `framework/assets`. Spec: `framework/spec/APPEARANCE-SOURCE.md`.
- Skins: every app has its own look (Nov 4 2026, Brett: "by default they're all their own." + "every one has a reset, restore to default."; build `skins`; replaces the "any look change applies to all" part of the rule above, the look still comes from axHub only): each app's slots, spacing and hidden chrome are in its own app-look@1 document on the hub (`shared/settings/looks/<app>.json`), snapshotted as that app's default when skins landed. A skin (skin@1, `framework/assets/skin/`, design packages read as skins too) is a layout + colour + style theme plus assets, switched on per app with Use skin (off by default); a pick with a skin on overrides just that part (Back to skin), and Restore to default puts the app back on its snapshot with a confirm and one undo. Settings → Appearance is the Theme manager in every app: one shared panel, `AppearancePanel` in `framework/libs/settings`. Control@1 token overrides (`axf.tokens.*`) still reach every app. CLI `node framework/cli/skins.mjs`, MCP through the theme-manager routes, CI `npx -y tsx framework/spec/check-skin.mts`. Format built on Opus, possible Fable review: plan `skins-possible-fab

## Rules for this job
- Fix what is broken when your tools can; anything that needs Brett goes in a systems check banner item with the exact steps, not only in chat.
- Tab rows are the framework TabGroup. Every toolbar has role="toolbar" and an aria-label. Checks: `node framework/cli/check-toolbars.mjs`, `node framework/cli/check-chrome-assets.mjs`.
- Plugin and library UIs conform to the theme engines (tokens only, framework layout primitives, `axf-<lib>` / `axp-<plugin>` naming, never define `--fx-*`); a plugin wanting its own look ships its own assets through the engines (scoping not built yet). The future plugin designer depends on this. Spec: `framework/spec/THEMING.md`. CI checks: `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` (static) and `apps/console-web/scripts/theme-swap.mjs` (switches every colour and style theme in the built console and fails on any colour or transparency that doesn't follow).
- Transparency is themed too: style themes carry `opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass` (→ `--fx-opacity-*`, same defaults on both ports). Translucent colours are `color-mix(in srgb, var(--fx-x) calc(var(--fx-opacity-…) * 100%), transparent)`, never a fixed percentage. `apps/demo` still has an older baked framework and needs a re-bake to get them.
- Console sizes are tokens (Oct 17 2026): `console.css` and the console views use `--fx-space`, `--fx-font-size`, `--fx-radius-*` and `--fx-border-w` (exact at the default soft-studio theme, so it looks pixel-identical there); the console is held to every theme rule. Shapes stay fixed: pill radii (999px), bar/chart heights, icon sizes.
- Build options are `--switches` on every build driver (CLI, engine-rpc, serve, console API/UI, MCP), defined only in `framework/schemas/build-options.json`; each sets an asset token, and new builds default every option off.
- `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` is the single source of truth for asset types. Per-port extensions live in files like `asset-types.android.json`.
- Cross-port: change a reference engine in framework/core, then regenerate framework/spec/fixtures. No new Android or Kotlin work: record the twin as a deferred gap in framework/spec/PORTING.md.
- React/TS port: the first React/TS app built on it sets the conventions, so it must stay engine-compatible for Android porting.
- `axf init` bakes `core/ react/ ui/ schemas/` into an app's `src/axf/` and records hashes in `axf.lock.json`. Change the framework, not baked copies.
- UI Review choices (Nov 7 2026): a build ships at least 3 options (ui-choices@1, `framework/core/ui-choices.mjs`), each a predicted look and an asset in `plugins/<owner>/assets/<type>/`, picked or not; Brett picks in the item's Choices tab, several in priority order where the type holds several views. smart-menus.brief:
# Build: smart-menus (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): "I need a dynamic context menu that draws itself depending on where it is and what it's doing. Most common / most likely things at the top. It learns and remembers, predicts what I'm most likely gonna want, keeps that at the top." Assigned agent: **Earl the Ear** (book on his card; if busy and the all-rounder router is on main, whoever is free - record who). Register in Urgent (id `smart-menus`) + banner entry.

## Build (framework level: every context menu in every app, existing and future)
- s1 **Context-aware drawing:** the context menu engine builds the menu at open time from: the target under the pointer (element kind, hook@1 / control@1 target, plugin, screen), its state (selected, running, failed, waiting on approval, has PR, etc.), the current screen, device (phone/desktop). Plugins contribute items with `when` conditions (state predicates) so irrelevant items never show; runtime context items stay the contribution path.
- s2 **Learning ranking, zero tokens:** record every pick locally + synced to axHub per user: (context key = target kind + state + screen, item id, time). Rank with frecency (frequency x recency decay) per context, plus time-of-day and 'what I just did' sequence boosts (simple Markov next-action counts). Top section 'Suggested' = top 3-5 predicted items; the rest grouped below in stable order so muscle memory still works. Plain code, NO LLM calls (test fails if the engine imports an LLM client).
- s3 Pinned items always first (from the pending `context-menu-editor` idea: user pins), then Suggested, then the rest; destructive items never auto-promoted to the top.
- s4 Settings (Settings > Menus, and a 'Menu settings' hook in every context menu): learning on/off, number of suggestions, reset learning (per menu / all), show why it's suggested (tiny hint), privacy: data stays on his axHub.
- s5 Works with menu-scroll (#268) placement and the toolbar build's hook@1/drop-target@1 if on main (don't edit their files). Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (get suggestions, reset, pin).
- s6 Tests (ranking math, context keys, when-conditions, reset, destructive never top), phone + desktop screenshots, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/smart-menus.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice, before start): dynamic SECTIONS, not the whole menu
Don't make the whole menu dynamic. Each context menu keeps its normal fixed items in their fixed order (muscle memory). Add dynamic SECTIONS on top of that:
- A 'Suggested' section at the top (learned/predicted items, 3-5, per s2) - can be turned off.
- A context section (items that only apply to this target/state, per s1 'when' conditions), clearly grouped.
- Pinned items (user pins).
The rest of the menu is static and never reorders. A menu asset declares which dynamic sections it shows and where; the default is Suggested at top + context section, static items below.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice): application menus too + 'what we're talking about' goes to the top
- The dynamic sections apply to the **application menu bar** too (every top-level menu: Builds, View, Tools, etc.), not just context menus. Permanent items stay fixed; each menu can declare dynamic sections.
- New dynamic section **'Talking about'** at the top of every menu (app menus + context menus): items relevant to what Brett and Amber (Claude) are currently talking about. Example: open Builds in the app menu while we're discussing the toolbar build -> that build (open it, its PR, its UI Review, its agent, stop it) is at the top.
- How it knows: add MCP tool `console_context` (policy ALLOW, navigation-only, no data change) on axf-console: {topics: [{kind: build|plugin|screen|pr|agent|setting|profile|note, id, label}], ttl_min?}. Amber calls it whenever the conversation moves to something (and console_show / follow-amber can feed it too). The console keeps a short rolling 'current topics' list per user (decays after ~30 min or when replaced), synced live to every open console client.
- Each menu maps topics to its relevant actions via plugins' contributed items with `when` conditions + the control@1 command registry (e.g. a build topic -> Builds menu shows Open build / Open PR / Open UI Review / Agent / Stop). Plain code, zero tokens.
- Settings > Menus: 'Talking about' section on/off, how long topics stay.
- Rule in shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'When the conversation moves to something in the console, call console_context with it.'

## Addendum 3 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice): all of it lives in ONE Menus plugin with tons of customization
- Everything in this build (dynamic sections in app menus + context menus, Suggested, Talking about, context section, pins, learning) is controlled by a **Menus plugin** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall, page + Settings > Plugins > Menus + a 'Menu settings' hook in every menu's context menu). Removing the plugin falls back to plain static menus.
- **Customization (tokens/assets only, saved per user on axHub, live preview, presets, reset, export/import as a menu-style asset):**
  - Colours: menu background, text, hover/selected, section headers, separators, icons, per-section accent (Suggested / Talking about / Pinned / context), badge colours, shadow, border, blur/glass, opacity.
  - Fonts: family, size, weight, letter spacing, section header style, icon size, density/row height, padding, corner radius, width min/max.
  - Animations: open/close (fade, scale, slide, drop, none), duration + easing, submenu reveal, item stagger, hover effect, highlight pulse for 'Talking about' items, reduced-motion respected.
  - Sections: order, on/off, max items each, labels, icons, collapse/expand, show 'why suggested' hint.
  - Behaviour: learning on/off + reset, topic lifetime, open on hover vs click (desktop), long-press time (phone), keyboard shortcuts.
  - Per-menu overrides (each app menu / context menu can have its own look and sections) from the hook in that menu.
- Works with menu-scroll (#268) placement and the Toolbars plugin (toolbar-tap-confirm build) through framework APIs - don't edit their files; share the hook@1 / drop-target@1 contract if it's on main.
- Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI (get/set menu settings, presets, reset learning, topics).

style-override-rule.said:
# Style override rule (Brett, Nov 7) — contract + enforcement

The rule:
1. Main apps — Dev Console, axHub web, AmberX, Patches — SHARE one style/theme/design. Their override switch is OFF by default.
2. Every plugin and every UI asset has its own override switch, ON by default. On first install it stores its own copy seeded from the shared style, so everything looks the same until someone changes it.
3. A plugin/asset override changes ONLY that plugin/asset. It never changes the app it belongs to, other plugins, or the shared style.
4. Turning a plugin's override OFF makes it follow its app's (shared) style live.
5. Turning an app's override ON gives that app its own style; its plugins keep their own copies.

Do:
- Find the existing pieces (app-style-override branch/build, apply-all-levels, appearance-asset-tokens, skins, theme engine, settings assets) and reuse them; finish app-style-override if it fits.
- Implement the resolution order in the shared theme/style engine (both web and Android twins where they exist): asset own copy (if override on) → app (if app override on) → shared main style.
- Switch in each app's and each plugin's settings (settings asset, no hard-coded UI). Migration: existing plugins get override ON with a copy of the current shared style; apps OFF.
- Write the rule to RULES.md and the brief template so every build follows it. CI check: every UI asset/plugin declares the override field.
- UI Review: submit the switch UI with three options (--choices).
- Tests for each rule above. Add to Shipped features.

Progress: append `<time> START|DONE <step>` to PROGRESS.md here at each step; don't stop between steps. Commit, don't push.

terminal-header-responsive.said:
The header on Terminal windows that open when a headless session starts (shows the output pane and the context chain) gets squished on smaller screens: items overlap.

1. Make the header measure its available width (ResizeObserver, not just viewport) and adapt live.
2. When space runs out, move items into a three-dots overflow menu, exactly like the top banner's overflow does. Reuse the same framework overflow control, don't build a new one.
3. Priority order for what stays visible (title/session name and status first); setting to choose which items stay pinned.

# Build: toolbar-tap-confirm (Urgent profile)

Brett, Nov 3 2026 (voice): every EXISTING and FUTURE toolbar uses the Terminal's Tooltip mode (first tap shows what the button does and arms it lit for 3 s, second tap within 3 s runs it, duration configurable; built in headless-tabs PR #259, s8). The double tap is ONLY on phones / touch. On a computer it stays a normal single click (hover tooltip as usual) - 'it really works on a computer.' Assigned agent: **Landin' Lenny** (book on his card; AXF_AGENT=landin-lenny if supported). Register in Urgent (id `toolbar-tap-confirm`) + banner entry.

## Steps
- s1 Lift Tooltip mode out of the Terminal plugin into the framework toolbar component (web reference + axf.css; Compose twin in PORTING.md unless trivial) as one shared behaviour; the Terminal uses the framework version (no duplicate code left in the plugin).
- s2 Device rule: double-tap confirm only when the input is touch (pointer: coarse / touch events / compact window class on a touch device). Mouse/trackpad/pen-hover = single click + hover tooltip. Decide per interaction (a touchscreen laptop: touch = double tap, mouse = single click).
- s3 Adopt everywhere: every toolbar in the console, every plugin, axHub web, AmberX (Capacitor), Molly, walkthrough-studio, templates/boilerplates, so new apps get it by default. Inventory every toolbar first and list them in the report.
- s4 Future-proof: the framework toolbar has it ON by default; a check (like check-controls) fails CI if any toolbar is built outside the framework toolbar or turns the behaviour off without an explicit, recorded reason. Add the rule to shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'Every toolbar uses tap-to-confirm on touch (framework toolbar); single click on desktop.'
- s5 Settings > Appearance (or Interaction): on/off for touch, arm duration (default 3 s); per-toolbar override only via the setting, not code. Destructive buttons keep their own confirm on top.
- s6 Tests (touch vs mouse paths, timeout, second tap on a different button re-arms instead of running), screenshots phone + desktop, UI Review item, report `_claude/builds/reports/toolbar-tap-confirm.md`, THREADS, PR, steps through the store. Commits clean and professional.
## Addendum 1 (Brett, Nov 3 2026, voice, before start): make all of this ONE Toolbars plugin
The framework toolbar becomes a **Toolbars plugin** (plugin@1, lifecycle install/uninstall) that owns every toolbar in every app, existing and future. Everything below is part of it.

### Settings
- Plugin settings (Settings > Plugins > Toolbars): global on/off for the touch double-tap tip (default on, phone/touch only), arm duration, defaults for all toolbars (theme, colours, density, icon size, labels on/off, position).
- **Every toolbar carries its OWN settings** (stored per toolbar id, synced via axHub like other settings): theming and colours (tokens/assets only: colour theme, style, background, button style, icon/label size, spacing, rounded/flat, opacity), layout (position, orientation, wrap vs scroll vs overflow menu, show/hide, auto-hide), behaviour (double-tap override for this toolbar, tooltips), and its button list.
- **Context-menu hooks on every toolbar** (right-click / long-press): 'Toolbar settings' (that toolbar's own settings), 'Edit toolbar' (opens the Toolbar editor), 'All toolbars...' (Toolbars plugin page that lists and controls every toolbar in the app). Contributed as runtime context items, so every existing and future toolbar gets them; CI check fails any toolbar without them.

### Toolbar editor
- Opens from the toolbar context menu. Add / remove / reorder / group / separators, edit each button (label, icon, tooltip text, action/hook, colour, visibility by level/role, keyboard shortcut), reset to default, undo/redo, live preview, save as an asset so it's hot-swappable and shareable.

### Drag and drop hooks anywhere
- A **hook** = any actionable thing in the app (menu item, nav item, toolbar button, banner item, 'Go to it' hooks, plugin commands from control@1 / plugin-commands-auto, settings pages, screens). Reuse the control@1 command registry and the pending `context-menu-editor` idea (save the action/destination, not the element).
- Drag any hook from anywhere and drop it on a **drop target**: any toolbar, the navigation menu, the banners, application menus, context menus, Home. Drag a button from one toolbar to another; nav menu -> toolbar and toolbar -> nav menu.
- On drop: a **configure dialog that depends on where it's dropped** (toolbar = new button dialog; nav menu = nav item dialog; banner = banner item dialog; menu = menu item dialog), prefilled with default values from the hook (label, icon, action, tooltip), with all the options for that target. Confirm creates it; move vs copy choice (default: copy from menus, move between toolbars), undo.
- Make it a framework contract: `drop-target@1` (what it accepts + which configure dialog) and `hook@1` (draggable action descriptor), open registries so any plugin/app can add targets and hooks without kernel changes. Phone: long-press to pick up, drag with edge auto-scroll, drop zones highlight.
- **Banners:** only add the banner drop target through the generic contract. Do NOT merge or rewrite banner-pack (#251), banner-editor (#254) or banners-one work; Brett is reviewing those himself. Note any overlap in the report.
- Rules: add to shared RULES.md + CLAUDE.md: 'Every toolbar is a Toolbars plugin toolbar: per-toolbar settings + editor via its context menu, tap-to-confirm on touch only, accepts dropped hooks.' Commands declared once -> REST + MCP + CLI.
- Split into clear steps in the store; tests for drop targets/dialogs/move-copy/undo, phone + desktop screenshots, UI Review items.

# Build: ui-registry-shortcuts

## Brett said (verbatim)
"Let's go with a UI shortcuts plugin. All the UIs need to be in a registry. Every single dialog, pop-up, settings interface, main plugin screen, every UI element has to be an asset. Every single asset in the whole app and all its plugins, from a button to a pop-up to a link to a menu to a menu entry, every thing needs to be an asset. That needs to be visible to the API." "Create a registry so I can open them with my voice."

1. Audit: list what is already an asset (chrome assets, settings-ui@1, tab-group@1, jump-menu@1, control@1 screens/dialogs, voice-command@1) and what isn't. Report the gap. Reuse existing contracts; don't duplicate control@1 or voice-command@1.
2. One UI registry (framework contract): every screen, dialog, pop-up, settings interface, menu, menu entry, button, link across console, AmberX, Molly, axHub web, and every plugin. Stable id, kind, owner app/plugin, label, aliases, how to open it. Plugins declare theirs; a scanner fills gaps; CI check that new UI is registered.
3. API/MCP/CLI: list, search, get, open/show/trigger any registered item.
4. Voice: UI Shortcuts plugin opens any registered item by voice (aliases, fuzzy match), wired to voice-command@1 and Gizmo; user-defined shortcuts.
5. Tests, README, report, screenshots to UI Review, PR to the merge queue. Do NOT land directly.

One session, lean chain. Stay out of Gizmo, badges, notifications code (other builds running).
## Addendum 1 (Brett, voice) - local assistant, no AI
"Without AI, I need an assistant that doesn't need Claude, that just knows my app. I should be able to tell it in plain English like: 'yo, make a notification to do this.'"
- Build a local, zero-token assistant on top of the UI registry + voice-command@1 + control@1: plain-English parsing with a grammar/intent matcher (no LLM), fuzzy matching, slots (names, times, on/off), confirmation for writes.
- It can: open any registered UI, change any setting, run any registered command, create/edit notifications and their style (through the notifications plugin's API), queue items for Claude (Gizmo queue) when the request really needs AI.
- Lives on the console; AmberX and Gizmo send it text/voice. 'What can I say?' lists commands. API/MCP/CLI.

## Addendum 2 (Brett, voice) - local LLM fallback
"Yes, we're gonna do that." (run a small local model through Ollama)
- The local assistant uses a small CPU model through Ollama (e.g. llama3.2:3b or qwen2.5:3b, ~4 GB RAM) ONLY as a fallback when the pattern matcher can't map the sentence: the model picks a command from the UI registry, never free-form actions. Zero Claude tokens.
- Share the Ollama install with the Gizmo rebuild (it installs Ollama + an embedding model for transcript RAG); don't install twice. Setting to turn the model off; memory limit; unload when idle.

## Steps
- s1 Feed: a `whats-new@1` feed built from what actually shipped: builds/steps whose code merged to main (store merged/mergedAt, merged PRs, build reports' Added/Changed sections, Codebase Changes plugin entries). Each item: title (plain-language feature, from the build report/PR, not commit-speak), build id, profile, apps affected (from changed paths: apps/console-web, axhub-web, amberx-droid, molly, plugins/<x> -> app/plugin names), date merged, deployed yes/no (deploy workflow run for that commit), links (PR, report). Server route + cached file; updates when the store/merges change (no model tokens).
- s2 Banner: a `whats-new` banner asset/widget (banner-pack conventions, works in the banner editor and gallery): compact ticker of the newest shipped features with an unread count; tap opens a panel.
- s3 Panel: list grouped by Date (Today / Yesterday / this week / older), By build, or By app (segmented switch, remembered); search; per-item details (what it does, where to find it, PR/report links); mark read / mark all read; 'new since last visit' highlighting.

- Tapping/clicking an item does NOT navigate; it only expands its details.
- Every **Live** item carries its own hook: a small 'Go to it' button/icon on the item.
